correctness.rationale: Every quantified d>=3 and 0<t<=1 is handled by an exact symmetry reduction: the John containment constraints A<=t and A^2+(d-1)B^2<=1 are necessary and sufficient by facet support; the Löwner constraints V>=1 and t^2/U^2+(1-t)^2/V^2<=1 are necessary and sufficient by the exhaustive vertex list. Strict one-variable and precision-space concave optimization produce globally unique optima. Nonnegative isotropic contact measures independently certify each ellipsoid at all branch boundaries. The logarithmic derivative of the exact ratio has a unique sign change because its two polynomial components are strictly oppositely monotone. Its d-asymptotic follows from the unique-root equation. The standalone verifier passed 88 finite configurations; no finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality of the combined exact one-coordinate-clipped cross-polytope theorem, two distinct contact changes, unique volume-ratio minimizer, and sharp d^(-1/4) law. The general symmetry/contact theory is explicitly pre-existing, and the directly relevant 2019 study of slabs of ℓ1 balls optimizes a different functional (intersection volume). Closest indexed ellipsoid records concern different body families; searched statements do not imply this exact classified profile. Residual risk: unindexed older special-case results, especially planar d=2 cases deliberately excluded.
residual_risks: No exhaustive worldwide historical-priority review; older planar ellipsoidal approximations or indexed differently described capped octahedra might exist.
General-purpose optimality criteria are classical, and originality attaches to this exact family, global ratio profile and asymptotic, not to those criteria.
A finite reproducibility checker does not independently validate the infinite proof; no external audit was performed.

value.rationale: The centrally and coordinate-symmetrically clipped ℓ1-ball is a canonical deformation removing exactly two opposite cross-polytope tips. The distinct John and Löwner contact thresholds produce a structurally nontrivial triple-piece exact ellipsoid-volume ratio. A unique, dimension-dependent best truncation and the sharp (2ed)^(-1/4) relative law quantify an unbounded d^(1/4)-order improvement over the untruncated cross-polytope. This is motivated shape approximation geometry, not a one-off arbitrary numeric slice.
